This article contains a **list of countries by length of coastline**, in kilometers. Though the coastline paradox stipulates that coastlines do not have a well-defined length, there are various methods in use to measure coastlines through ratios and other metrics. A coastline of zero indicates that the country is landlocked.




## Overview[edit]


![](image)
![](image)
An example of the coastline paradox. If measured using an interval of 125 mi (200 km), the coast of Great Britain has a length of about 1,500 mi (2,400 km). Using an interval of 30 mi (50 km), the length is about 2,100 mi (3,400 km).


</fragment>
<fragment>
11. **^** In 1900, the Dutch coastline measured approximately 1400 km. It has significantly been reduced by the closing of the Zuiderzee by the Afsluitdijk in 1932 (250 km) and the closing of several sea arms by the Delta Works (700 km).
12. **^** Israel has an additional coastline along the Dead Sea and the Sea of Galilee (both landlocked), with a total length of 63 km.
13. **^** Excluding Ascension Island (data unavailable).
14. **^** Includes Baker Island, Howland Island, Jarvis Island, Johnston Atoll, Kingman Reef, Midway Atoll, and Palmyra Atoll.
15. **^** Figure represents the coastline of the entire island, including Sint Maarten (administered by the Netherlands).
16. **^** Jordan has an additional 50 km of coastline along the Dead Sea, which is landlocked.
17. **^** Coastline included in figure for Saint Martin (administered by France).
18. **^** Kazakhstan has a coastline with the Caspian Sea, which is landlocked, with a total length of 1,894 km.

</fragment>
<fragment>

1. **^** The smaller the scale interval mathematically, the more detailed and the "greater the scale of the map", in common usage. See scale (map).
2. **^** World total includes countries not listed and coastline for disputed areas.
3. ^ ***a*** ***b*** ***c*** ***d*** ***e*** Includes coastline of outlying islands.
4. **^** Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark.
5. **^** Russia has an additional 850 km of coastline along the Caspian Sea, which is landlocked.
6. **^** Includes coastline length for the Canary Islands.
7. **^** Excludes minor outlying islands.
8. **^** Does not include Saint Paul Island and the Crozet Islands (data unavailable) or the Adelie Land claim to Antarctica.
9. **^** Iran has an additional 740 km of coastline along the Caspian Sea, which is landlocked.
10. **^** Includes coastline in the Gulf of Fonseca (163 km).

</fragment>
</document>

<document>
<title>Coastline of Australia</title>
<content>
![](image)Satellite photo of Australia
![](image)Tallow Beach, Byron Bay, New South Wales
The **coastline of Australia** comprises the coasts of mainland Australia and Tasmania. It nominally includes a part of all Australian states and territories; the otherwise landlocked Australian Capital Territory has a coastal enclave at Jervis Bay Territory.


According to *The World Factbook*, Australia has the sixth longest coastline in the world, at 25,760 kilometres (16,010 mi).[1][2]


Due to the historical context of European discovery and exploration, the coastline has been the first point of contact over 400 years.[3]


In the IBRA bioregionalisation, the coast has 36 coastal bioregions that define the whole coast[4]
and there is the more complex Integrated Marine and Coastal Regionalisation of Australia, which includes ecological features that are beyond the shoreline.




## History

[edit]

For thousands of years, Indigenous Australian clan groups along the coastline have preserved a longstanding maritime tradition in connection of sea country, with the conservation of marine life across large areas of Australia.


In the period of the European maritime exploration of Australia, the Australian coastline was discovered by a group of navigators, including Willem Janszoon, Dirk Hartog, Abel Tasman, Captain James Cook and Matthew Flinders, who went on to become the first in leading the first inshore circumnavigation of Australia and charter much of the coast.


The Australian Maritime Safety Authority promotes the protection of the marine environment and the infrastructure of safety for navigation around the coastline, which maintains a national search and maritime rescue services.


The coast of Australia preserves two of its world heritage sites inscribed by UNESCO, including the Ningaloo Coast and the Great Barrier Reef.

**Highest points (mountains) in the five countries with the longest coastlines**

| Rank (by coastline length) | Country | Highest point (mountain) | Elevation* | Where it lies |
|----------------------------|---------|---------------------------|------------|----------------|
| 1 | **Canada** | **Mount Logan** | 5 959 m (19 551 ft) | Yukon, part of the Saint Elias Mountains |
| 2 | **Norway** | **Galdhøpiggen** | 2 469 m (8 100 ft) | Jotunheimen range, central Norway (mainland) |

| 4 | **Russia** | **Mount Elbrus** | 5 642 m (18 510 ft) | Western Caucasus, Kabardino‑Balkar Republic |
| 5 | **Australia** | **Mawson Peak (Heard Island)** – **or** Mount Kosciuszko (mainland) | 2 745 m (9 006 ft) – Mawson Peak; 2 228 m (7 310 ft) – Kosciuszko | Mawson Peak is on Heard Island (Australian external territory in the Southern Ocean); Mount Kosciuszko lies in the Snowy Mountains of New South Wales (mainland) |

- Coastline lengths (used for the ranking) are those reported by the CIA World Factbook and other standard references:

- For Australia the “highest point of the country” is technically Mawson Peak on the Australian external territory of Heard Island. If one restricts the answer to the continental mainland, the well‑known highest summit is Mount Kosciuszko. Both are listed for completeness.
